rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 7 (sensors at x ±0.03 m, y 0.08 m, 12 mm footprints, kp 3.8, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 1.3, last_direction) is the best raced design at 687.06. Iteration 9 narrowed the spacing to ±0.02 m and scored 676.7. The oval and s-bend still finished 20/20, but slalom progress fell from 0.449 to 0.365 and line-loss events rose to 1.4. That falls below the 687 threshold the Evaluator set, so the fallback rule applies. Narrow spacing is ruled out. Widening (iteration 6) and narrowing (iteration 9) both lowered slalom progress, so ±0.03 m is the best lateral spacing found so far.

What is ruled out: kp 4.0 (slalom progress 0.46 to 0.44), kd 0.8 vs 0.7 (kd helps the s-bend but cuts slalom progress), base_speed 1.2 (cost more on the oval and s-bend than it gained), y 0.06 vs 0.08 (y 0.08 helped overall), a 16 mm footprint (neutral, 685.5, with slalom progress down). The gain and sensor-geometry levers have been tried around this design.

Change (one variable from iteration 7): mass 0.8 kg to 0.6 kg. The yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, so a lighter robot turns faster for the same steering command. The slalom has sign changes that the robot cannot follow in time, and the lower inertia may reduce overshoot past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Lower mass should also reduce slip and rolling resistance. Everything else is held at iteration 7: geometry (x ±0.03, y 0.08, 12 mm, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.12 x 0.18), and the controller (base_speed 1.3, kp 3.8, ki 0, kd 0.8, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction).

Expected result: slalom progress above 0.45 and max_error at or below 0.06, with the oval and s-bend still 19/20 or better. Risk: the lighter robot may change the effective gain, so the oval or s-bend oscillation could rise. Fallback: if the score falls below 687, or the oval drops to 18/20 or below, or s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.37, iteration 11 reverts to the iteration 7 design exactly (mass 0.8). Do not adjust gains to rescue it.

Hypotheses: (a) slalom failure is partly yaw-inertia lag, so lower mass raises slalom progress; (b) the oval finish is unaffected because its curvature is gentle. Measurements requested: all metrics, with per-track slalom progress, max_error and line_loss_events, and s-bend steering_oscillation, compared against iteration 7.
